items.title: Jeanette Kimball Interview, 1962-02-10
items.q: I still believe in that written work and the catechism and the scales by all means. Because it gives dexterity. ... And as I said before, I owe everything to my first teacher. ... Mrs. Stewart. ... Anna. Anna Stewart.

ctx.x: Well, it takes a lot of study, I can say that. But the young people don't want to study. That's right. They want to begin playing right away. But I still like that method of catechism and written work and all those sort of things. And when you're learning music. It has paid off for me. I wouldn't give anything for it. But of course the music pupils of today want to go right to the piano and begin playing. But how are you going to play if you don't know the basic things about music? So my advice would be to learn…
And what is her name again now? Mrs. Stewart. What was her first name? Anna. Anna Stewart. And she's still living in New Orleans.
Yes, she's still living in New Orleans. Although she has retired. But she was a graduate of the Boston Conservatory. And she was wonderful.
